svg.title: We explain the identification with the actual run, since it is needed for the order of quantifiers in the theorem. The run’s stage profile is the original profile, its kernel is the original kernel, and its factor at profile j is the length just selected. Hence (CAL12) at J(m + 1) is the actual step’s local length inequality. Its stationary horizon satisfies the original primary price list. Projecting the two maxima in (CAL15) gives each local patch payment, and therefore its stationary admissibility and the delay required for the flat covariance limit. The preselected flat supplier may now be applied with entrance index zero to this very horizon; the curvature and dual suppliers apply to it by the other two floors. Their local results concern the same levels, patches and retained horizon as the run. No new family is chosen when these numerical payments are consumed. The finite volume and token comparisons are established afterwards on this fixed run, and only then is a requested extraction order refined.
